### Create new variables

#### Survey variables and sociodemographic characteristics

```{r}
df <- brfss23 %>% mutate(
  
  # create indicator for overall summary
  one = 1,
  
  # survey data variables
  # this syntax helps make the survey design object later
  strata = `_STSTR`,
  weight = `_LLCPWT`,
  
  # sex
  sex =  factor(x = SEXVAR,
                levels = c(2, 1),
                labels = c("Female", "Male"),
                ordered = FALSE),
  
  # age
  age = case_when(`_AGEG5YR` == 14 ~ NA, # missing
                  `_AGEG5YR` %in% c(1, 2) ~ 1, # 18–29 
                   `_AGEG5YR` %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ 2, # 30–44
                  `_AGEG5YR` %in% c(6, 7) ~ 3, # 45–54
                  `_AGEG5YR` %in% c(8, 9) ~ 4, # 55–64
                  `_AGEG5YR` %in% c(10, 11) ~ 5, # 65–74
                  `_AGEG5YR` %in% c(12, 13) ~ 6, # ≥ 75 years
                  TRUE ~ NA),
  
  age = factor(x = age,
               levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
               labels = c("18–29", "30–44", "45–54", "55–64", "65–74", "≥75"),
               ordered = FALSE),
  
  # race/ethnicity
  raceeth = case_when(
    `_RACE` == 9 ~ NA,
    TRUE ~ `_RACE`),
  raceeth = factor(x = `_RACE`,
                levels = c(3, 4, 2, 8, 7, 5, 1, 6),
                labels = c("American Indian or Alaskan Native, non-Hispanic",
                           "Asian, non-Hispanic", 
                           "Black, non-Hispanic",
                           "Hispanic", 
                           "Multiracial, non-Hispanic",
                           "Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander, non-Hispanic",
                           "White, non-Hispanic", 
                           "Another single race, non-Hispanic"),
                ordered = FALSE),
  raceeth_hispanic = factor(x = `_RACE`,
                levels = c(8, 3, 4, 2, 7, 5, 1, 6),
                labels = c("Hispanic", 
                           "American Indian or Alaskan Native, non-Hispanic",
                           "Asian, non-Hispanic", 
                           "Black, non-Hispanic",
                           "Multiracial, non-Hispanic",
                           "Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander, non-Hispanic",
                           "White, non-Hispanic", 
                           "Another single race, non-Hispanic"),
                ordered = FALSE),
  # education level
  edu = case_when(
    `_EDUCAG` == 9 ~ NA,
    TRUE ~ `_EDUCAG`),
  edu = factor(x = `_EDUCAG`,
               levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
               labels = c("Did not graduate high school",
                          "Graduated high school",
                          "Attended college or technical school",
                          "Graduated from college or technical school"),
               ordered = FALSE),
  
  # BMI
  bmi = factor(x = `_BMI5CAT`,
               levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
               labels = c("Underweight",
                          "Normal weight",
                          "Overweight",
                          "Obesity"),
               ordered = FALSE),
  
  # MSA status
  msa = case_when(
    is.na(`_METSTAT`) ~ NA,
    TRUE ~ `_METSTAT`),
  msa = factor(x = msa, 
               levels = c(1, 2),
               labels = c("Metropolitan counties",
                          "Nonmetropolitan counties"),
               ordered = FALSE),
  msa_nonmetro = factor(x = `_METSTAT`, 
               levels = c(2, 1),
               labels = c("Nonmetropolitan counties",
                          "Metropolitan counties"
                          ),
               ordered = FALSE)
  )
  
# check

# Return a list with factor levels and numeric codes for each factor column
lapply(df[ , sapply(df, is.factor)], function(v) {
  data.frame(Levels=levels(unique(sort(v))),
             Values=as.numeric(unique(sort(v))))
  })

# cross tabs between coded and original variables
df %>% tabyl(sex, SEXVAR)
df %>% dplyr::group_by(age, `_AGEG5YR`) %>% tally() %>% arrange(`_AGEG5YR`) %>% print(n = 20)
df %>% dplyr::group_by(raceeth, `_RACE`) %>% tally() %>% arrange(`_RACE`)
df %>% dplyr::group_by(raceeth_hispanic, `_RACE`) %>% tally() %>% arrange(`_RACE`)
df %>% dplyr::group_by(edu, `_EDUCAG`) %>% tally() %>% arrange(`_EDUCAG`)
df %>% dplyr::group_by(bmi, `_BMI5CAT`) %>% tally() %>% arrange(`_BMI5CAT`)
df %>% dplyr::group_by(msa, `_METSTAT`) %>% tally() %>% arrange(`_METSTAT`)
df %>% dplyr::group_by(msa_nonmetro, `_METSTAT`) %>% tally() %>% arrange(`_METSTAT`)
```

#### Physical activities 
```{r}

# meeting aerobic PAG and most common activities
## this code creates a new column for each activity, and participants can report up to two activities (so can have response of 1 for max of two columns)

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(
    pag_aerobic = case_when(
      `_PA150R4` == 9 ~ NA, 
      TRUE ~ `_PA150R4`),
    pa_no = case_when( # no past-month PA
      EXERANY2 == 1 ~ 0,
      EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 1,
      .default = NA
    ),
    pag_aerobic = factor(x = pag_aerobic,
               levels = c(1, 2, 3),
               labels = c("150+ minutes/week",
                          "1-149 minutes/week",
                          "0 minutes/week"),
               ordered = FALSE), 
    walking = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 1 | EXRACT22 == 1) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    running = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 2 | EXRACT22 == 2) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    gardening = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 3 | EXRACT22 == 3) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    bicycling = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 4 | EXRACT22 == 4) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    aerobics = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 5 | EXRACT22 == 5) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    calisthenics = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 6 | EXRACT22 == 6) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    elliptical = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 7 | EXRACT22 == 7) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    household = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 8 | EXRACT22 == 8) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    weightlifting = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 9 | EXRACT22 == 9) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    yoga = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 10 | EXRACT22 == 10) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0),
    other = case_when(EXERANY2 == 2 ~ 0, # no PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ NA, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
                        EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 == 11 | EXRACT22 == 11) ~ 1, 
                        TRUE ~ 0)
    )

# check for walking
df %>%
  group_by(walking, EXERANY2, EXRACT12, EXRACT22) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>% 
  print(n=999)

df %>% tabyl(`_PA150R4`, pag_aerobic)
df |> tabyl(EXERANY2, pa_no)

```

#### Inclusion indicator
```{r}

#TODO clean this up and check
# inclusion/exclusion
df <- df %>% 
  mutate( 
    # exclusion is based on activities
    include = case_when( # TODO check this
      EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ FALSE, # don't know or refused for PA in past month
      EXERANY2 == 2 & complete.cases(sex) ~ TRUE, # include those with reported no past-month PA and have sociodemographic data
      EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 %in% c(77, 99)) ~ FALSE, # yes for past-month PA, refused or don't know for first activity, they are all missing data for second activity
      .default = TRUE), # otherwise, include
    exclude = case_when( # TODO need to fix this to match the code above
      EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) ~ "1. don't know, refused, or missing for past-month PA (EXERANY2)", # don't know or refused for PA in past month
      !(SEXVAR %in% c(1, 2)) ~ "2. missing sex data",
      EXERANY2 == 1 & (EXRACT12 %in% c(77, 99)) ~ "2. refused for first activity (EXRACT12), not asked about second", # refused or don't know for first activity, don't answer EXRACT22 #TODO check this one
      .default = "4. include") # otherwise, include
    ) 

# sample flow
df %>% tabyl(exclude, include)
df %>% tabyl(exclude)

# those with missing data for EXRACT12 also have missing for EXRACT22
df %>% filter(!(EXERANY2 %in% c(7, 9, NA) | (EXERANY2 == 2 & complete.cases(sex, age, raceeth, edu, bmi)))) %>% filter(is.na(EXRACT12)) %>% tabyl(EXRACT22)

# no respondent with NA for EXRACT12 if EXERANY2==1
df %>% tabyl(EXERANY2, EXRACT12)

# all but 1 who have 77 or 99 for EXRACT12 are missing for EXRACT22. There is one with EXRACT12==1 and EXRACT22 is missing (who in included)
df %>% filter(EXERANY2==1) %>% tabyl(EXRACT12, EXRACT22)
df %>% filter(EXERANY2==1 & EXRACT12==1 & is.na(EXRACT22)) %>% select(include)
df %>% filter(EXERANY2==1) %>%  # yes past month PA
  filter(EXRACT12 %in% c(77, 99)) %>% # refused or don't know for first activity
  tabyl(EXRACT22) # all missing data for EXRACT22


# check variables for included vs excluded
df %>% group_by(include) %>% 
  skimr::skim(sex, age, raceeth, edu, bmi, msa,
              # `_PA150R4`, pag_aerobic,
              pa_no,
              walking:other,
              EXERANY2, EXRACT12, EXRACT22)
  
```

## Setup for weighted analyses

### Create survey design object using srvyr
```{r}
# https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/data/Tutorials/Code/DB303_R.r
# https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/2019/pdf/Complex-Smple-Weights-Prep-Module-Data-Analysis-2019-508.pdf

# Set options for allowing a single observation per stratum
options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust")

# Create survey design using srvyr package 
brfssdsgn <- df %>%
  as_survey_design(ids = 1, # 1 for no cluster ids
                   weights = weight, # weight variable created above
                   strata = strata) # sampling was stratified

```

### Subset

```{r}

# Subsetting the original survey design object ensures we keep the design information about the number of clusters and strata
subset <- subset(brfssdsgn, include == 1)

# subset by sex
subset_female <- subset(brfssdsgn, include == 1 & sex == "Female")
subset_male <- subset(brfssdsgn, include == 1 & sex == "Male")
```

## Create functions

### Overall prevalence for sample characteristics

```{r}
# function for sample characteristics

# TODO might need to add some code to include the missing values?
# subset$variables$bmi <- addNA(subset$variables$bmi)

overallPrevalence <- function(var,
                              text = NULL,
                              design){

  # formulas
  formula_var = as.formula(paste("~", var))
  formula_one = as.formula("~ one")
  
  # if variable is a factor
  if (design$variables[[var]] %>% is.factor()){
    
    # row with header for characteristic
    header <- data.frame(characteristic = text)
    
    # get unweighted n
    n <- svyby(formula = formula_one, by = formula_var, design = design, 
               unwtd.count,
               na.rm.by = TRUE, na.rm.all = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>% 
      rename(characteristic = var) %>% 
      select(characteristic, counts) %>% 
      `rownames<-`(NULL)  
    
    # get overall percentage/mean
    mean <- svyby(formula = formula_var, by = formula_one, design = design, 
                  svymean,
                  keep.var = TRUE, vartype = "se",
                  na.rm.by = TRUE, na.rm.all = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
      select(starts_with(var)) %>% 
      pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
                   names_to = "characteristic",
                   values_to = "mean") %>%
      mutate(characteristic = stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(characteristic, # remove suffixes for later merge
                                               pattern = var, 
                                               replacement='',
                                              vectorize=FALSE))
    
    # get SE
    se <- svyby(formula = formula_var, by = formula_one, design = design, 
                  svymean,
                  keep.var = TRUE, vartype = "se",
                  na.rm.by = TRUE, na.rm.all = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
      select(starts_with("se.")) %>% 
      pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
                   names_to = "characteristic",
                   values_to = "se") %>%
      mutate(characteristic = stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(characteristic, # remove suffixes for later merge
                                               pattern = paste0("se.", var), 
                                               replacement='',
                                              vectorize=FALSE))
    
     # get CI corresponding to overall percentage/mean 
     ci_l <- svyby(formula = formula_var, by = formula_one, design = design, 
                 svymean,
                 keep.var=TRUE, vartype="ci",
                 na.rm.by = TRUE, na.rm.all = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
       select(starts_with("ci_l")) %>%
       pivot_longer(cols=c(starts_with("ci_l")),
                    names_to = "characteristic",
                    values_to = "ci_l") %>%
       mutate(characteristic = stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(characteristic,
                                                pattern=c('ci_l\\.', var),
                                                replacement='',
                                                vectorize=FALSE))
     
     ci_u <- svyby(formula = formula_var, by = formula_one, design = design, 
                 svymean,
                 keep.var=TRUE, vartype="ci",
                 na.rm.by = TRUE, na.rm.all = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
       select(starts_with("ci_u")) %>%
       pivot_longer(cols=c(starts_with("ci_u")),
                    names_to = "characteristic",
                    values_to = "ci_u") %>%
       mutate(characteristic = stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(characteristic,
                                                pattern=c('ci_u\\.', var),
                                                replacement='',
                                                vectorize=FALSE))
    
    # combine n, mean, and CIs
     output <- bind_rows(header,
                         plyr::join_all(list(n, mean, se, ci_u, ci_l), by = "characteristic")) %>%
       mutate(
         # https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/2023/pdf/Compare_2023-508.pdf
         suppress = case_when(
           counts < 50 ~ "1. small n",
           se/mean > 0.3 ~ "2. wide RSE",
           TRUE ~ "3. present data"
         ),
         display = case_when(
           # display estimate and 95% CI if not suppressed
           is.na(counts) ~ "", # make empty for header
           suppress != "3. present data" ~ "—",
           TRUE ~ paste0(formatC(mean * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
                                   " (", 
                                   formatC(ci_l * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
                                   "–", 
                         formatC(ci_u * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"), 
                                   ")")
         ))
  
  # if variable is logical
     } else if (design$variables[[var]] %>% is.numeric()){
       
       # unweighted n for numerator
       n <- svyby(formula = formula_one, 
                  by = formula_var, 
                  design = design,
                  unwtd.count,
                  na.rm.by = TRUE, na.rm.all = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>% 
         filter(.data[[var]]==1) %>% 
         select(counts)
       
       # weighted
       mean <- svyby(formula = formula_var,
                     by = formula_one,
                     design = design, 
                     svymean, 
                     vartype = c("ci", "se")) %>% 
         select(-one)
       
       output <- bind_cols(n, mean) %>%  # combine
         mutate(suppress = # suppression flag
                  case_when(
                    counts < 50 ~ "1. small n",
                    se/.data[[var]] > .3 ~ "2. large RSE",
                    TRUE ~ "3. present data"),
                display = # estimate and 95% CI if not suppressed
                  case_when(
                    suppress !="3. present data" ~ "—",
                    TRUE ~ paste0( # concatenate estimates and CIs
                      formatC(.data[[var]] * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
                      " (",
                      formatC(ci_l * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
                      "–",
                      formatC(ci_u * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
                      ")"))) %>%
         rename(mean = .data[[var]]) %>%  # rename to be able to combine later
         mutate(characteristic = text) %>% # new col with name of activity
         `rownames<-`(NULL) # remove named index
       }

  return(output)
}

```

### Stratified estimates for physical activities

```{r}
# function to get unweighted n, weighted prevalence mean (95% CI), weighted chi-sq for categorical

stratifiedPrevalence <- function(outcome, var, text = NA, design) {
  # formulas
  formula_var = as.formula(paste("~", var))
  formula_outcome = as.formula(paste("~", outcome))
  mean_text <- paste0(outcome, "TRUE")
  ci_low <- paste0("ci_l.", outcome, "TRUE")
  ci_up <- paste0("ci_u.", outcome, "TRUE")
  
  # unweighted n
  n <- svyby(
    formula = formula_outcome,
    by = formula_var,
    design = design,
    unwtd.count,
    na.rm.by = TRUE,
    na.rm.all = TRUE,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) %>%
    rename(characteristic = var) %>%
    select(characteristic, counts) %>%
    `rownames<-`(NULL)
  
  # weighted mean and CI
  ci <- svyby(
    formula = formula_outcome,
    by = formula_var,
    design = design,
    svymean,
    vartype = "ci",
    na.rm.by = TRUE,
    na.rm.all = TRUE,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) %>%
    rename(characteristic = var,
           mean = outcome) %>%
    `rownames<-`(NULL) %>% 
    select(characteristic, mean, ci_l, ci_u)
  
  # weighted SE for mean
  se <- svyby(formula = formula_outcome, by = formula_var, design = design, 
                  svymean,
                  keep.var = TRUE, vartype = "se",
                  na.rm.by = TRUE, na.rm.all = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>% 
    rename(characteristic = var) %>% 
    select(characteristic, se) %>% 
    `rownames<-`(NULL) 

  # # for overall estimates
  # if (var == "one"){
  #   output <- left_join(n, ci) %>% 
  #     mutate(characteristic = text,
  #            pvalue = NA,
  #            suppress = case_when( # suppression flag
  #              counts < 50 ~ "1. small n",
  #              ci_u - ci_l > 0.05 &
  #                ((ci_u - ci_l) / mean > 1.3) ~ "2. wide absolute and relative CI width ", # TODO change to SE
  #              TRUE ~ "3. present data"), 
  #            prev = case_when( # display estimate and 95% CI if not suppressed
  #              suppress != "3. present data" ~ "—",
  #              is.na(mean) ~ "",
  #              TRUE ~ paste0(
  #                # concatenate estimates and CIs
  #                formatC(mean * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
  #                " (",
  #                formatC(ci_l * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
  #                "–",
  #                formatC(ci_u * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
  #                ")"
  #              )
  #            )
  #     )
  #   # for subgroup estimates, get weighted p-value for chi-sq test
  # } else {
    output <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(
      characteristic = text,
      p.value = svychisq(as.formula(paste0("~", outcome, "+", var)), design, statistic =
                      "adjWald")$p.value %>% as.numeric()),
    plyr::join_all(list(n, ci, se), by = "characteristic")) %>%
    mutate(
      pvalue = case_when(
        p.value >= 0.001 ~ formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f"), #3 decimals for p-value
        p.value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
        TRUE ~ ""
      ),
      suppress = # suppression flag
        case_when(
          counts < 30 ~ "1. small n",
          se/mean > 0.3 ~ "2. wide RSE",
          TRUE ~ "3. present data"
        ),
      prev = # present estimate and 95% CI if not suppressed
        case_when(
          suppress != "3. present data" ~ "—",
          is.na(mean) ~ "",
          TRUE ~ paste0(
            # concatenate estimates and CIs
            formatC(mean * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
            " (",
            formatC(ci_l * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
            "–",
            formatC(ci_u * 100, digits = 1, format = "f"),
            ")")
        ),
      display = # column with either pvalue or prevalence
        case_when(
          pvalue != "" ~ pvalue, 
          prev != "" ~ prev,
          TRUE ~ "")
    )
    # }
  
  return(output)
}
```

### Pairwise comparisons

#### List the comparisons and test results
```{r}

# pairwise testing
comparison <- function(var, outcome, design) {
  
  # Ensure that 'var' is a factor
  design[[var]] <- as.factor(design[[var]])
  
  # Create a formula for svyttest
  formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", var))
  
  # Get the levels of the variable
  levels <- levels(df[[var]])
  
  # Check if there are enough levels to compare
  if (length(levels) < 2) {
    stop("Not enough levels to compare.")
  }
  
  # Generate all pairs of levels
  pairs <- combn(levels, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  # number of pairs (needed later for Bonferroni correction)
  pairs_number <- pairs %>% length()
  
  # Calculate p-values for each pair
  results <- map_dfr(pairs, ~ {
    comparison_name <- paste(.x, collapse = " vs ")
    
    # Subset the design dataframe for the current pair
    subset_data <- design %>% filter(!!sym(var) %in% .x)
    
    # Check if subset_data is empty
    if (nrow(subset_data) == 0) {
      warning(paste("No data for comparison:", comparison_name))
      return(tibble(comparison = comparison_name, pvalue = NA))
    }
    
    # Perform the svyttest
    p.value <- svyttest(formula, subset_data)$p.value
    
    # format p-value with Bonferroni correction and add asterisk if stat. sig.
    pvalue <- case_when(
        p.value >= 0.05/pairs_number ~ formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f"),
        p.value >= 0.001 & p.value < 0.05/pairs_number ~ paste0(formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f"), "*"),
        p.value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001*",
        TRUE ~ "")
    
     # Determine if the p-value is statistically significant with Bonferroni correction
    stat_sig <- case_when(
        is.na(p.value) ~ NA,
        p.value >= 0.05/pairs_number ~ FALSE,
        p.value < 0.05/pairs_number ~ TRUE)
    
    # Return the results in a tibble
    tibble(comparison = comparison_name, pvalue = pvalue, stat_sig = stat_sig)
  })
  
  return(results)
}
```

#### Add superscripts for table

```{r}
# function to list the subgroup with superscripts for the for pairwise survey t-tests with Bonferroni correction  

## start argument is which number (corresponding to order of letters of the alphabet) to use for superscripts. For example, start = 2 would start superscripts with "b"

comparison_superscript <- function(var, outcome, design, start = 3) {
  
  # Ensure grouping variable is factor
  design$variables[[var]] <- as.factor(design$variables[[var]])
  
  # # ----------------------------
  # # Outcome preparation
  # # ----------------------------
  #   <- unique(na.omit(design$variables[[outcome]]))
  # 
  # if (all(outcome_vals %in% c(1, 2))) {
  #   design$variables[[outcome]] <- ifelse(design$variables[[outcome]] == 1, 1,
  #                                         ifelse(design$variables[[outcome]] == 2, 0, NA))
  #   design$variables[[outcome]] <- as.logical(design$variables[[outcome]])
  #   
  # } else if (all(outcome_vals %in% c(0, 1))) {
  #   design$variables[[outcome]] <- as.logical(design$variables[[outcome]])
  #   
  # } else {
  #   warning(paste("Unexpected outcome coding in", outcome))
  # }
  
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create Formulas, get levels of var, and establish pairs 
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", var))
  levels_var <- levels(design$variables[[var]])
  
  if (length(levels_var) < 2) stop("Not enough levels to compare.")
  
  pairs <- combn(levels_var, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  bonf_cutoff <- 0.05 / length(pairs)
  
  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Calculate Pairwise survey t-tests / p_values
  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  pairwise_results <- map_dfr(pairs, ~ {
    
    g1 <- .x[1] # 1st group to compare
    g2 <- .x[2] # 2nd group to compare
    comparison_name <- paste(.x, collapse = " vs ") # text to describe which groups are compared
    
    # Subset the design data.frame for the current pair    
    subset_data <- subset(design, design$variables[[var]] %in% .x) # previously c(g1, g2)), but .x is cleaner
    
    # Perform the svyttest
    p.value <- svyttest(formula, subset_data)$p.value
    
    # format p-value to 3 decimal places, show "<0.001" if below that  / add asterisk if significant
    pvalue <- if (!is.na(p.value)) {
      if (p.value < 0.001) {
        formatted <- "<0.001"
      } else {
        formatted <- formatC(p.value, digits = 3, format = "f")
      }
      if (p.value < bonf_cutoff) paste0(formatted, "*") else formatted
    } else {
      NA_character_
    }
    
    tibble(
      variable = var,
      outcome = outcome,
      group1 = g1,
      group2 = g2,
      comparison = comparison_name,
      pvalue = pvalue,
      stat_sig = ifelse(!is.na(p.value) & p.value < bonf_cutoff, TRUE, FALSE),
      bonferroni_cutoff = bonf_cutoff
    )
  })
  
  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Work toward adding superscripts based on the testing
  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  
  # Create a matrix to track connections between groups
  connection_matrix <- matrix(FALSE, nrow = length(levels_var), ncol = length(levels_var),
                              dimnames = list(levels_var, levels_var))
  
  # Fill the connection matrix based on significant pairwise results
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairwise_results))) {
    if (!is.na(pairwise_results$stat_sig[i]) && pairwise_results$stat_sig[i]) {
      g1 <- pairwise_results$group1[i]
      g2 <- pairwise_results$group2[i]
      connection_matrix[g1, g2] <- TRUE
      connection_matrix[g2, g1] <- TRUE
    }
  }
  
  # Create a list to hold the superscripts for each group
  final_superscripts <- tibble(
    # variable = var,
    characteristic = levels_var,
    superscript = setNames(as.list(rep("", length(levels_var))), levels_var)
  )
  
  # Assign letters for superscripts
  
  end = nrow(pairwise_results) + start - 1
  letters_used <- letters[start:end]
  letter_counter <- 1
  
  # Assign superscripts based on connections 
  for (i in seq_along(levels_var)) {
    for (j in seq_along(levels_var)) {
      if (i < j && connection_matrix[i,j]) {
        final_superscripts$superscript[i] <- str_c(final_superscripts$superscript[i], letters_used[letter_counter])
        final_superscripts$superscript[j] <- str_c(final_superscripts$superscript[j], letters_used[letter_counter])
        letter_counter <- letter_counter + 1
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Combine the results with the pairwise results
  output <- final_superscripts %>%
    mutate( #outcome = outcome,
           superscript = unlist(superscript))
  
  if (any(is.na(output$superscript))) {
    warning(paste("Missing values in superscript columns"))
  } else {
    return(output)
  }
  
}
```

```{r}
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "raceeth", text = "Race and ethnicity", design = subset_female),
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "edu", text = "Education level", design = subset_female),
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "msa", text = "Metropolitan Status", design = subset_female),
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "bmi", text = "Body Mass Index category", design = subset_female))  |> 
  full_join(
    bind_rows(
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "age", design = subset_female),
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "raceeth", design = subset_female),
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "edu", design = subset_female), 
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "bmi", design = subset_female),
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "msa", design = subset_female)),
    by = join_by(characteristic)) |>   
  select(characteristic, 
         # counts, 
         prev,
         superscript) |> 
  rename(#counts_female = counts,
         prev_female = prev,
         superscript_female = superscript)

# males only
tbl3_male <- bind_rows(
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "age", text = "Age group (years)", design = subset_male),
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "raceeth", text = "Race and ethnicity", design = subset_male),
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "edu", text = "Education level", design = subset_male),
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "msa", text = "Metropolitan Status", design = subset_male),
    stratifiedPrevalence(outcome = "walking", var = "bmi", text = "Body Mass Index category", design = subset_male))  |> 
  full_join(
    bind_rows(
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "age", design = subset_male),
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "raceeth", design = subset_male),
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "edu", design = subset_male),
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "bmi", design = subset_male),
      comparison_superscript(outcome = "walking", var = "msa", design = subset_male)),
    by = join_by(characteristic)) |>   
  select(characteristic, 
         # counts, 
         prev,
         superscript) |> 
  rename(#counts_male = counts,
         prev_male = prev,
         superscript_male = superscript)

# join
tbl3 <- full_join(tbl3_total,
                  tbl3_female,
                  by = join_by("characteristic")) |>
  full_join(tbl3_male,
            by = join_by("characteristic"))

# make flextable
tbl3_ft <- tbl3 %>% 
  flextable() %>%
  compose(part = "body",
    i = ~ superscript_total != "",   # only rows needing superscript
    j = 'prev_total',
    value = as_paragraph(
      as_chunk(prev_total),
      as_sup(superscript_total))) %>% 
  compose(part = "body",
    i = ~ superscript_female != "",   # only rows needing superscript
    j = 'prev_female',
    value = as_paragraph(
      as_chunk(prev_female),
      as_sup(superscript_female))) %>% 
  compose(part = "body",
    i = ~ superscript_male != "",   # only rows needing superscript
    j = 'prev_male',
    value = as_paragraph(
      as_chunk(prev_male),
      as_sup(superscript_male))) %>%
  delete_columns(c("superscript_total", "superscript_female", "superscript_male")) %>%
  set_header_labels(
    characteristic = "Characteristic",
    prev_total = "Total",
    # counts_female = "n",
    prev_female = "Females",
    # counts_male = "n",
    prev_male = "Males") %>%
  add_header_row(values = c("", 
                            "% (95% CI)"), 
                 colwidths = c(1, 3)) %>% 
  add_header_row(values = paste0("Table 2. Weighted prevalence of walking among adults, Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System — United States, 2023"),
                 colwidths = tbl3 %>% ncol() - 3) %>%
  italic(i = c(which(tbl3$prev_female == "")), # italics for readability
         j = 1) %>% 
  padding(i = c(which(tbl3$prev_female != "")), # indent for readability
          j = 1,
          padding.left = 20) %>%
  padding(padding.top = 0, padding.bottom = 0) %>% 
  flextable::footnote(i = 1,
                      j = 1,
                      part = "header",
                      value = as_paragraph(c("If participants reported any past-month, non-occupational physical activity, they then listed the types of the two activities they spent the most time doing in the past month. Walking was the most frequently reported of the two physical activities they spent the most time in the past month doing.")), 
                      ref_symbols = c("a")) %>%
  flextable::footnote(i = 3,
                      j = 1,
                      part = "header",
                      value = as_paragraph(c("Participants missing data on a characteristic were excluded from analysis of that characteristic.")), 
                      ref_symbols = c("b")) %>%
    add_footer_lines(
      value = as_paragraph(
        as_sup("c-o"),
        "Within a characteristic for each column, subgroup pairs with the same superscript letters are significantly different (p <0.05, Bonferroni-corrected pairwise t-tests).")) %>% 
  autofit(add_w=0) %>%
  flextable::fontsize(size = 10, part="all") %>%
  font(part="all", fontname = "Arial") %>% 
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit") %>% 
  theme_vanilla()

tbl3_ft
```

### Pairwise comparisons. These tables wil not be in the paper, but we will add symbols to Table 2 depicting the statistically significant differences.

#### Among females

```{r}

tbl2_pairwise_female <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(comparison = "Age group (years)"),
  comparison(var = "age", outcome = "walking", design = subset_female),
  data.frame(comparison = "Race and ethnicity"),
  comparison(var = "raceeth", outcome = "walking", design = subset_female),
  data.frame(comparison = "Education level"),
  comparison(var = "edu", outcome = "walking", design = subset_female),
  data.frame(comparison = "Body Mass Index category"),
  comparison(var = "bmi", outcome = "walking", design = subset_female),
  data.frame(comparison = "Metropolitan status"),
  comparison(var = "msa", outcome = "walking", design = subset_female)) %>%
  filter(stat_sig %in% c(NA,TRUE)) %>% 
  select(-stat_sig)

# make into flextable
tbl2_pairwise_female_ft <- tbl2_pairwise_female %>% 
  flextable() %>%
  add_header_row(values = as_paragraph("Statistically significant pairwise comparisons for FEMALES for Table 2"),
                 colwidths = ncol(tbl2_pairwise_female)) %>% 
  set_header_labels(comparison = "Characteristic and comparisons",
                    pvalue = "p-value") %>% 
  italic(i = c(which(is.na(tbl2_pairwise_female$pvalue))),
         j = 1) %>% 
  padding(i = c(which(tbl2_pairwise_female$pvalue != "")),
          j = 1,
          padding.left = 20) %>%
  flextable::footnote(i = c(1),
                      j = c(1),
                      part = "header",
                      value = as_paragraph(c("The asterisk (*) denotes statistical significance in t-testing with Bonferroni correction.")),
                      ref_symbols = c("a")) %>%
  padding(padding.top = 0, padding.bottom = 0) %>% 
  flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part="all") %>%
  font(part="all", fontname = "Arial") %>%
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit") %>% 
  theme_vanilla()
```

# Modeling

## Entire sample
```{r}
# mutivariable logistic regression
model_total <- (svyglm(walking ~ sex + age + raceeth_hispanic + edu + bmi + msa,
                       family = quasipoisson(log),
                       design = subset,
                       na.action = na.omit))
```

## Females
```{r}

model_female <- (svyglm(walking ~ age + raceeth_hispanic + edu + bmi + msa_nonmetro,
                        family = quasipoisson(log),
                        design = subset_female,
                        na.action = na.omit))

# jtools::summ(model_female, confint = T)
# summary(model, correlation = TRUE) 

# get df of aORs and CIs
fig1_female_aors <- exp(cbind(OddsRatio = coef(model_female), # exponentiates coef to get OR
                           confint(model_female))) %>% # get CIs
  data.frame() %>% # make into dataframe
  mutate(statsig = case_when(X97.5.. <1 & X2.5.. <1 ~ TRUE, # label for below null
                             X97.5.. >1 & X2.5.. >1 ~ TRUE, # above null
                             TRUE ~ FALSE), 
         referent = FALSE, # label for figure
         female_display = paste0( # text in manuscript of OR & CI
           formatC(OddsRatio, digits = 2, format = "f"),
           " [",
           formatC(X2.5.., digits = 2, format = "f"),
           "–",
           formatC(X97.5.., digits = 2, format = "f"),
           "]")) 
# clean: add columns for variable name
fig1_female_aors$var <- rownames(fig1_female_aors)
fig1_female_aors$var <- sub("sex|raceeth_hispanic|edu|age|msa_nonmetro|bmi", "", fig1_female_aors$var) # remove category name
fig1_female_aors <- fig1_female_aors %>% filter(var != "(Intercept)") # not intercept

# # remove the ones we need to suppress based on table 1
# # TODO recode if this changes
# fig1_female_aors <- fig1_female_aors %>% 
#   filter(!var %in%
#            c("American Indian or Alaskan Native, non-Hispanic",
#              "Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander, non-Hispanic",
#              "Another single race, non-Hispanic"))

# add index
fig1_female_aors <- tibble::rowid_to_column(fig1_female_aors, "index_asc")

# df for referent groups
fig1_female_ref <- data.frame(index_asc = c(0.5, 8.5, 12.5, 15.5, 19.5),
                           var = c("18–29",
                                   "Hispanic",
                                   "Did not graduate high school",
                                   "Underweight",
                                   "Nonmetropolitan counties"),
                               OddsRatio = 1,
                               X2.5.. = 0,
                               X97.5.. = 0,
                               female_display = "Referent",
                               statsig = FALSE,
                               referent = TRUE,
                               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# combine with aORs, sort by index, create new index
# fig1_female_aors <- fig1_female_aors %>% select(index, var, OddsRatio, X2.5.., X97.5.., female_display, statsig)# df for white space
fig1_female_blank <- data.frame(index_asc = c(0.45, 5.45, 12.45, 15.45, 18.45), 
                             var = c("Age group (years)", 
                                     "Race and ethnicity", 
                                     "Education level", 
                                     "Metropolitan status",
                                     "Body Mass Index category"))
fig1_female <- bind_rows(fig1_female_aors, fig1_female_ref, fig1_female_blank) %>% arrange(desc(index_asc))
fig1_female <- fig1_female %>% 
  mutate(index = rank(-index_asc)) %>%  # descending for figure
  select(-index_asc)

# display
fig1_female %>% filter(!is.na(var)) %>% arrange(desc(index)) %>% select(var, female_display, statsig) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  set_caption("Text for manuscript for walking aORs among females") %>% 
  set_header_labels(var = "Characteristic",
                    female_display = "aOR for walking among females",
                    statsig = "p-value<0.05?") %>%
  bold(i = ~ statsig == TRUE, bold = TRUE) %>%
  autofit(add_w=0) %>% 
  theme_vanilla()

fig1_female_plot <- ggplot(fig1_female, aes(x = OddsRatio, y = index, color = statsig, shape = referent)) + # plot OR, different color if stat. sig.
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1), linewidth = .25, linetype = "dashed") + # line for null
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmax = X97.5.., xmin = X2.5..), linewidth = 1, height = .5) + # error bars
  geom_point(stroke= 3.5) + # size of dot
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # background lines 
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = fig1_female$index, labels = fig1_female$var) + # y-axis
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(.5, 1, 2, 2.5), 
                     labels = c(.5, 1, 2, 2.5), 
                     limits = c(.5, 2.5)) + # x-axis
  coord_transform(x = "log10") + # x-axis log scale
  ylab("") +
  xlab("aPORs (Log Scale)") +
  ggtitle(str_wrap("Walking among females", width=37)) +
  theme(legend.position="none") + # no legend
  scale_color_manual(values = c("gray65","black")) # color of dots

fig1_female_plot

rm(fig1_female_aors, fig1_female_ref, fig1_female_blank)

```
